THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioners are before this Court calling in question an order dated 30.08.2024, passed by the IV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, in P.C.R.No.8537/2024 and consequent registration of a crime in Crime No.271/2024, for the offences under Sections 506, 34, 120B, 406,
408, 419, 420 and 307 of the IPC.
NC: 2024:KHC:51589 2.

Heard Sri Shyam Sundar M.S., learned senior counsel along with Smt. Vandana P.l., learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri B.N.Jagadeesha, learned Additional State Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 and Sri D.R.Ravishankar, learned senior counsel for Sri J.N.Naveen, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.
Respondent No.2 is the complainant, who registers a private complaint invoking Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. in P.C.R.No.8537/2024.
The private complaint was filed on 24.05.2024.

Before the Mr Vasudevan Sathyamoorthy vs State By Halasuru P S on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61652859/

sentences.text:
concerned Court, respondent No.2 files a memo, which reads as follows:
"MEMO The undersigned counsel for the complainant herewith submitting to this Hon'ble Court praying that the above case may kindly be transferred to the jurisdiction court under section 192(2) of Cr.P.C. in the interest of justice."

The complainant himself would project that the concerned Court has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the complaint petition and therefore, seeks transfer of the complaint to the NC:
2024:KHC:51589 jurisdictional Court under Section 192(2) of the Cr.P.C.
Notwithstanding the memo filed by the complainant, the concerned Court refers the matter for investigation under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. and a crime is registered in Crime No.271/2024.
It is these order and the registration of the Crime that has driven the petitioners to this Court in the subject petition.

4. Learned senior counsel for the petitioners submits that that the concerned Court had admittedly no jurisdiction to entertain the complaint and it is also the case of the complainant that the concerned Court that had no jurisdiction to entertain the private complaint.
Therefore, the concerned Court ought to have transferred the matter to the appropriate Court having jurisdiction instead of referring the matter for investigation.

5. Learned senior counsel representing both the parties would submit that the order be set aside and the matter be remitted to the appropriate Court to consider the issue and NC: 2024:KHC:51589 pass necessary orders by referring the matter for investigation or otherwise.
6. In the light of the aforesaid submissions, the impugned order dated 30.08.2024 requires to be obliterated and the matter to be remitted to the jurisdictional Court.

In the event, the learned Magistrate would come to a conclusion that the matter would require investigation, the jurisdictional Court shall follow the procedure stipulated under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'the BNSS') and regulate its procedure.

7. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER a.
The writ petition is allowed.
b. The order dated 30.08.2024, passed by the IV Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru, stands quashed.
The consequent registration of the FIR in Crime No.271/2024 shall stand obliterated.

d. The private complaint filed by the complainant be placed before the appropriate Court and if appropriate Court opines that the matter requires investigation, the procedure under the provisions of the BNSS, 2023, shall be followed.
